JUDGMENT:
-
Challenge in this MACMA is to the award, dated 26.04.2016 in M.V.O.P.No.744 of 2013, on the file of the Chairman, Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal-cum-I Additional District Judge, Guntur ("Tribunal" for short), whereunder the Tribunal dealing with a claim for compensation of Rs.3,00,000/- made by the petitioner on account of the injuries sustained by him in a motor vehicle T S Rao, Guntur Dist vs P Nageswara Rao 2 Others

1 accident, which was occurred on 06.06.2013, awarded a sum of Rs.1,80,000/-.
2)
The parties to this MACMA will hereinafter be referred to as described before the Tribunal for the sake of convenience.
3) The case of the petitioner, in brief, according to the averments set out in the claim before the tribunal, is that the petitioner is resident of Kovelamudi, Guntur District.
On 06.06.2013 at about 8-00 p.m., the petitioner was proceeding on a motorcycle from Mutluru to Kovelamudi on main road.

When he reached near Danthala Katta, the third respondent, who is the driver of auto bearing No.A.P.16-TV-4435 (hereinafter will be referred to as "offending vehicle"), drove the auto in a rash and negligent manner and hit the motorcycle of the petitioner.
The petitioner received multiple fractures.
He was admitted in a private hospital at Guntur.
A case in Crime No.45 of 2013 under Section 337 of the Indian Penal Code was registered by the Station House Officer, Vatticherukuru Police Station against the third respondent.
The petitioner is an agricultural coolie at the time of accident and he is getting Rs.200/- per day.
He underwent operations by spending huge amount.
He sustained disability which is a permanent one.

The first respondent is owner, the second respondent is insurer and the third respondent is driver of the offending vehicle and they are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.

4) The first respondent got filed a written statement contending in substance that the alleged accident was occurred only due to the negligent act of the petitioner, who was proceeding on his motorcycle in the middle of the road and there is no negligence on the part of the driver of offending vehicle.
The offending vehicle is insured with the second respondent.
The driver of offending vehicle is having valid and effective driving licence.
So, the second respondent alone is liable to pay compensation.
The compensation claimed by the petitioner is highly excessive, unreasonable and illegal.
5) The second respondent got filed a written statement contending in substance that the petitioner is put to strict proof about all the allegations made in the petition.
The accident occurred was due to collision of two vehicles, but the petitioner has not impleaded the owner and insurer of the motorcycle.
The accident was occurred on 06.06.2013 but the report was given to the police on 10.06.2013.
The compensation claimed is excessive and exorbitant.
6) The third respondent remained exparte.

7) On the basis of the above pleadings, the tribunal settled the following issues for trail:
(1) Whether the accident was occurred due to rash and negligent driving of driver of auto rickshaw bearing No.A.P.16-TV-4435 and caused injuries to Thota Srinivasa Rao on 06.06.2013 at about 8- 00 p.m.?
(2) Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation and if so, to what amount and from whom?
T S Rao, Guntur Dist vs P Nageswara Rao 2 Others on 7 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/5233436/
2 (3) To what relief?
8) During the course of enquiry, on behalf of the petitioner, P.W.1 and P.W.2 were examined and Ex.A.1 to Ex.A.8 were marked.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: On behalf of the contesting second respondent R.W.1 was examined and Ex.B.1 and Ex.B.2 were marked.

9) The tribunal on hearing both sides and considering the oral as well as documentary evidence answered the issues in favour of the petitioner and against the respondents and awarded a sum of Rs.1,80,000/- towards compensation with interest at 7.5% per annum thereon from the date of petition till the date of deposit.

Feeling that the compensation so awarded is not just and reasonable,
the petitioner filed the present MACMA.

10) Insofar as the finding of the tribunal that the accident occurred was on account of the rash and negligent driving made by the driver of the offending vehicle is concerned, those are not sought to be disturbed by the respondents by filing any cross objections.
So the scope of the appeal is limited.

11) Hence, in deciding the present MACMA, the point for determination is whether the award, dated 26.04.2016in M.V.O.P.No.744 of 2013, on the file of the Chairman, Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal- cum-I Additional District Judge, Guntur, in awarding compensation of Rs.1,80,000/- as against the original claim of Rs.3,00,000/-, is sustainable under law and facts and whether there are any grounds to enhance the compensation?

entities.text: Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal- cum-I Additional District Judge, Guntur
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
POINT:-
12) Sri N. Nagaraju, learned counsel, representing Sri A. Rajendra Babu, learned counsel for the appellant, would contend that the petitioner produced a medical certificate showing the disability as that of 67%, but the tribunal considered the disability as 25% alone.

The tribunal should have considered the disability as claimed and no compensation was awarded towards attendant charges and extra nourishment and other incidental expenses, as such, compensation needs to be enhanced accordingly.

13) Sri Srinivasa Rao Vutla, learned counsel for the second respondent, would canvass the contention that the tribunal took over care to see that just and right compensation is awarded to the petitioner, as such, there is no need to interfere with the award of the tribunal.
14) As seen from the evidence of P.W.1, he filed chief examination affidavit in tune with the pleadings and through his examination Ex.A.1 to Ex.A.8 were marked.
15) The petitioner examined P.W.2, the doctor, who treated him and according to the evidence of P.W.2, he is practising as Consultant Orthopaedic Surgeon in Yashaswi Hospitals, Guntur.
On 06.06.2013 the petitioner was admitted in their hospital due to injuries received in the road accident and the petitioner received type-II compound T S Rao, Guntur Dist vs P Nageswara Rao 2 Others

3 fracture of right femur and right tibia involving right knee joint.
The injured was operated on 07.06.2013 and he was discharged on 17.06.2013.
They issued Ex.A.5-discharge summary.

The petitioner has difficulty in bending the right knee joint due to the said injuries and he was unable to sit cross legged and in squatting position and he cannot stand without support and he cannot walk longer distance.
The disability is at 50% to 55% which is permanent and partial.
He testified that the expenditure for the treatment as Rs.40,000/-.
16) It is to be noted that insofar as the injuries sustained by the petitioner is concerned, there is no dispute.
The petitioner produced only Ex.A.6 showing an amount of Rs.10,473/- towards medical expenditure.
However, the tribunal considered the evidence of P.W.2 and awarded a sum of Rs.25,000/- towards medical expenses and conveyance charges.
Hence, the contention of the petitioner that the tribunal did not award proper amount under the head of transport charges deserves no merits.
The tribunal awarded a sum of Rs.20,000/- towards pain and suffering.
The petitioner produced Ex.A.7-disability certificate as if he sustained disability of 67%, but P.W.2 testified that the disability is 50% to 55%.
The tribunal took into consideration the fact that it is not a case of amputation.
The tribunal considered that the disability spoken to by P.W.2 is also higher side.

Hence, the tribunal considered the fact that as there was compound fracture of right femur and right tibia involving right knee joint, the disability can be fixed as 25%.
17)
It is to be noted that whenever a disability certificate is produced, it is the bounden duty of the tribunal to consider the disability as that of whole body.
The tribunal made such exercise and rightly fixed the disability as 25%.

The tribunal considered the monthly income of Rs.3,000/- thereby Rs.36,000/- per annum and considering the age applied multiplier "15" and arrived at the loss of earnings to a tune of Rs.1,35,000/- i.e., Rs.36,000/-x25%x15.
So, even the exercise made by the tribunal to ascertain the loss of earnings to a tune of Rs.1,35,000/- is just and reasonable.
18) It is a fact that the tribunal did not award any amount towards extra nourishment and loss of earnings during the period of treatment.
Though the petitioner did not claim it, but it is the duty of the tribunal to award some amount towards extra nourishment.
It is a case of disability of 25% the petitioner was in the hospital from 06.06.2013 to 17.06.2013.
The nature of injuries are also such that the petitioner was supposed to have some bed rest.

Considering the same it is just and reasonable to award some amount towards loss of earnings i.e., Rs.3,000/- + Rs.3,000/- (i.e.,
Rs.6,000/-) for a period of two months.
Further looking into the nature of injuries, the petitioner was supposed to have a special diet for speedy recovery and a sum of Rs.10,000/- appears to be reasonable towards extra nourishment.
Hence, the compensation needs to be enhanced to a tune of Rs.16,000/- as above.

19) In the result, the MACMA is allowed in part with proportionate costs enhancing the compensation from that of Rs.1,80,000/- to Rs.1,96,000/- and the respondents shall deposit the difference amount of Rs.16,000/- with interest at 7.5% per annum from the date of petition till the date of deposit within a period of one month from this day.

On such deposit, the petitioner is T S Rao, Guntur Dist vs P Nageswara Rao 2 Others on 7 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/5233436/
4 entitled to withdraw the entire amount in lump sum.
